question: An operations manager has finished a long planning chat and expects the team to revisit the same topic every month. What is the best way to keep that context available?
options: A) Rely on Claude recalling the earlier planning chat automatically whenever she opens a new conversation.
B) Keep reopening the same long chat every month so that all of the history stays inside one conversation.
C) Copy the whole transcript into the first message of every monthly chat so that nothing at all is ever left out.
D) Save the agreed decisions into a Project as knowledge, then start each monthly review as a fresh chat there.
correct_answers: D) Save the agreed decisions into a Project as knowledge, then start each monthly review as a fresh chat there.
explanations: Incorrect. Automatic recall is not a dependable store for decisions the team must rely on months later; durable context should be persisted into project knowledge deliberately.
Incorrect. A conversation that grows for a year will keep condensing its own earlier content and will draw heavily on usage allowance.
Incorrect. The transcript is mostly working discussion rather than durable fact, and re-pasting it each month wastes window space and allowance.
Correct. Persisting the durable output into project knowledge keeps the context available to every future chat without carrying months of transcript inside one conversation.
